parallel.requirements: Recognized the full Transform Arena bootstrap: restore Vector3, Matrix, Quaternion, and Point math; repair ReplayIO, ReplayRunner, SimWorld, QuaternionSystem; generate replay artifacts and acceptance reports.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent restored engine math and launched one workflow panel for game-side reconstruction, while retaining final integration, commits, tests, and artifact generation ownership.
parallel.implementation: Implemented game-side ReplayIO and ReplayRunner fixes and used workflow-derived or manually reconciled SimWorld and QuaternionSystem code after discovering sibling edits to the shared files.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Stopped the workflow when children edited shared game files directly, then manually inspected diffs, committed requirement patches, and attempted output generation in the same workspace.
parallel.verification: Ran local checks and direct run-tests, but official evaluation records agent_timeout and final_test_results null; harness only shows direct run-tests exited with 1 and patches were collected.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official final test result set exists for parallel because the agent timed out; the collision-disrupted game-side workflow left reconciliation and acceptance incomplete at closure.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same eight requirement slugs and final artifact obligations, including deterministic replay, engine trace flags, math event stream, and hash generation.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Worked serially across three rounds with workflows and delegation tools disabled; one local actor retained implementation, integration, testing, and final reporting ownership.
serial.implementation: Restored Point, Vector3, Matrix, and Quaternion math; implemented ReplayIO, SimWorld, QuaternionSystem, and ReplayRunner; removed the seed increment and emitted quaternion trace state.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Committed all eight non-empty requirement patches, regenerated the expected output artifacts, and delivered a final response summarizing coverage and the remaining reference-hash mismatch.
serial.verification: Reported local engine, replay, and agent tests; official tests confirmed most outputs and math traces but failed the same-seed replay determinism/hash acceptance item.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Serial still failed official evaluation because final replay/hash determinism did not match the reference expectation, even though it reached official testing and completed all requirement patches.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run had the same full bootstrap prompt: restore XNA Vector3/Matrix math, repair game replay components, build tests, run two replays, and emit required artifacts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had the same requirements and ultimately reported all eight requirement slugs reviewed and implemented before evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition gap is proven; the difference is that serial continued through all requirements while parallel timed out after a disrupted workflow and manual reconciliation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed engine and game-side work, delegating replay_io, sim_world, quaternion_system, and replay_runner_fix as a workflow child task while the parent remained the integrator.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all implementation local across three rounds with workflows disabled and no child logs or task-stop lifecycle.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced shared child ownership over game files; serial avoided cross-agent ownership and retained one local writer/integrator path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Workflow children received briefs naming the game-side files and requirements, then observed that siblings had already edited or were editing the same files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child handoff boundary; it carried task context through one local workspace and summarized the underdetermined hash problem at closure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel context issue was not a missing brief or lost handoff; it was current workspace state becoming unstable across live children, which serial did not create.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced edits to game-side files and later committed all eight requirement patches, but the parent had to verify and reconcile unexpected shared-file modifications.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial reported canonical engine math and game-side implementations for Point, Vector3, Matrix, Quaternion, ReplayIO, SimWorld, QuaternionSystem, and ReplayRunner.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both touched the same substantive requirement surface, but serial reached a cleaner final implementation path and official tests while parallel finished through collision-disrupted manual edits.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent launched the workflow, then explicitly stopped it after observing direct edits; protocol validation records the workflow was stopped rather than retrieved normally.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial has no child result lifecycle; the last round returned normally and wrote a final response describing requirement coverage and residual mismatch.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost a normal workflow result lifecycle and had to take over; serial had no comparable join, retrieval, or stopped-child boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Multiple live workflow children observed sibling edits to the same game files, and the parent stopped the active workflow because panel agents were editing files directly.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial workflows were disabled and no delegation or subagent activity appears in protocol validation, so game-file edits came from one local actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the core strategy difference: parallel created a same-file shared-state collision, while serial avoided live cross-agent writes entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel official evaluation completed with failure_mode agent_timeout and final_test_results null after direct run-tests exited with 1.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial official evaluation reached the test suite: required outputs, math events, trace checks, hash formatting, and engine tests passed, while same-seed replay determinism failed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel did not reach a usable final official test result set; serial reached official tests and failed a specific determinism/hash acceptance point.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed one long round with 11 workflow child logs and ended at timeout after stopping the workflow and taking over shared-file edits.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used three rounds, with the final round process_ok true and a final response documenting 8/8 reviewed and implemented before evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure pressure was amplified by the stopped shared-file workflow; serial spent more rounds but closed with a coherent local artifact set and only the hidden/reference hash mismatch unresolved.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both runs failed officially, but not in the same way. Parallel introduced an executed workflow for game-side code, suffered live same-file edits among child agents, stopped the workflow, and then timed out without final official test results. Serial kept one local owner across three rounds, completed all eight requirement patches, and reached official evaluation, where the remaining visible failure was the replay determinism/hash acceptance check.
parallel_contributors: Workflow children collided on shared game-side files, forcing the parent to stop the workflow and manually reconcile the edits.
The parallel run ended with agent_timeout and null final_test_results, so it did not produce a completed official acceptance result set.
serial_contributors: Serial avoided cross-agent shared-file writes by running with workflow and task tools disabled.
Serial completed all eight requirement patches and reached official tests, but the final replay hash/determinism acceptance still failed.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The serial residual failure is an implementation/acceptance mismatch around replay hash determinism rather than a coordination label.
Parallel may also contain ordinary implementation defects, but official evaluation does not expose final testcase-level failures because the run timed out.
evaluator_effects: The current status evaluation is authoritative for pass/fail; testcase count fields in the sidecar are null under the provided resolver although serial status lists individual final_test_results.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: Supported comparative contributors for a both-fail pair; the retained pattern is adverse but not claimed as an outcome-differential root cause.
